chapter_theme: The inner religion (உட்சமயம்): the six sects are roads to one city and the Lord made them all, so quarrelling over which is good is a dog barking at a hill; within them Nandi set one Saiva path of the guru, Hara's path, which knowers and gods cannot reach by examining alone but which opens to those who worship his feet.
structure_note: 1557 and 1558 state the thesis about the six sects; 1559 to 1567 describe Hara's path and Nandi's Saiva way; 1568 returns to mocking those who rank penances; 1569 to 1572 turn to the Lord's faces, his inclusion of all deities and the hidden use of the body.

1557.reading: The ancient First One who long ago shaped both the gods and us is the First Lord who moves among the six sects so that they seek his pair of feet.
1557.nuance: அமையங்கு உழல்கின்ற is unclear: 'roams there among them' or 'is fitly there'. On either reading the six sects are his arrangement, not rivals to him.

1558.reading: As one great city has six roads leading to it, so are the six sects; those who say 'this is good, that is bad' are like a dog that rises barking at a hill.
1558.nuance: The hill is unmoved by the barking: the quarrel harms only the quarreller. The verse does not say every road is equally short; 1556 and 1567 show Tirumular still ranks a Saiva path.

1559.reading: Come and reach, and be saved by, the unique Lord of Saiva greatness, Nandi the bright flame who gives life so that souls are saved, loving to those of true greatness, lord of the world who gives bliss.
1559.nuance: சைவப் பெருமை names the Saiva path in a chapter that has just told sects not to rank one another; the inner religion is offered as fulfilment, not as a rival sect.

1560.reading: For those able to know, by seeking the way he laid down within the divine path Siva set, that 'this one is he', he is there, and it becomes a duty.
1560.nuance: பவன் may be Bhava, a name of Siva, and பழிவழி (the way of blame) may be a corruption of பழவழி (the old way). இவன் அவன் is often taken as recognizing the soul as one with the Lord, or the guru as the Lord; the verse does not settle which.

1561.reading: For the six sects that teach how to become, there is no way to go except merit; for other souls, the way there is the flowering creeper of the supports.
1561.nuance: ஆதாரப் பூங்கொடியாள், the flower-creeper lady of the ādhāras, is taken as Shakti or kundalini rising through the body's centres. The verse seems to set the sects' road of merit against an inner yogic road, but the syntax is loose.

1562.reading: Even in the days when I knew Hara's path and still wandered searching other paths, the solitary flame stood on the strong path by which one crosses the sea of the heart and climbs.
1562.nuance: The verse is autobiographical: the Lord was already waiting on the path while the speaker strayed. உரநெறி and தரநெறி (the strong path, the path of rank or crossing) are unclear.

1563.reading: The Siva path that reached the discerned Hara, the great way by which those who turned away went in contemplation, the path of grace by which the fulfilled entered the beyond, coming and adorning it, becomes the path of union.
1563.nuance: The verse piles up names for one path; பேர்ந்தவர் (those who moved away, from the world or from births) and போந்து புனைந்து are uncertain.

1564.reading: Cast off the divided mind so that its twoness ends; recite the moving letter ச, and reciting, abide in Hara's path and contemplate; then the flame-light that fills will appear.
1564.nuance: சகாரம், the letter ச, is traditionally the first letter of சிவாய and so stands for Siva in the five-letter mantra; ஊரும் (moving) may describe the breath carrying it. ஈரும் மனம் is the mind that splits or cuts.

1565.reading: If you see the Lord whose sign is lightning, whose sign in the Brahmins' Veda is fire, the First Lord whose sign is thought, the dear sign at the tip of the shoot of knowledge, that is Hara's path.
1565.nuance: The four குறி (signs) may be forms of the inner light; மினல் is read as மின்னல், lightning. நயக்குறி and ஞானக் கொழுந்து (the tip, or flame, of knowledge) are obscure.

1566.reading: Hara's path stands so that souls, many though they are, cannot grasp it by examination; those who plunge in, worship his red feet with folded hands and, being worn away, understand, find it a bliss.
1566.nuance: ஆன்மாச் சதுர்பல is obscure: perhaps 'souls of four and many kinds'. தேய்ந்துணர் may be 'understand as the self wears away'. The contrast between examining and plunging in is clear and recurs in 1571.

1567.reading: Nandi, the unique Lord of the Saiva religion, laid down one guru's path for salvation: the divine Siva path, the true way, which he set out for those in the world to join and be saved.
1567.nuance: சன்மார்க்கம், the true path, is in later Siddhanta the highest of four paths (after charya, kriya and yoga); whether Tirumular uses it in that technical sense here can't be fixed from this verse.

1568.reading: Our great Nandi laughs when he sees madmen who give two names, 'this penance' and 'that penance'; whatever the penance, wherever one is born, those who understand alike can quickly enter the city.
1568.nuance: ஒல்லை ஊர் is 'quickly, the city', echoing the one city of 1558. எங்குப் பிறக்கிலென் sets birth aside as well as sect.

1569.reading: The Lord has five faces and is the precious soul; the Lord has a sixth face turned downward; for the Lord and his garland of skulls, we ourselves are the Lord's human nature.
1569.nuance: The five faces are Sadasiva's; அதோமுகம், the downward face, is a sixth in some Agamic accounts. சிரமாலை may be a garland of heads (skulls) or a garland on his head. The last line is very obscure; I read it as the Lord taking human nature in us, but that is a guess.

1570.reading: The First Lord who measured the seven worlds stands as the tidal sea and as all lives; Parasakti, standing undivided, is the deity of the beginning and the end.
1570.nuance: உலகேழும் அளந்தவன், who measured the worlds, is Vishnu's epithet as Trivikrama; applied to the First Lord it fits the chapter's case that other sects' gods are his. Whether ஆதிப்பிரான் here is Vishnu, Siva or both can't be fixed.

1571.reading: Gods and vidyadharas examine and know, yet Hara's path stands beyond their examining; I examined and knew to worship his red feet, and examining and knowing, I saw this life and the next.
1571.nuance: ஆய்ந்தறி opens every line: the same examining that fails the gods succeeds when it ends in worship. இம்மை அம்மை is this life and the other.

1572.reading: The use of the body, which cannot be known, he made into six unknowable kinds; in the six unknowable sheaths an unknowable cosmos is set.
1572.nuance: அறியவொண்ணாத (cannot be known) opens every line. கோசம் is kosha, a sheath of the self; the usual count is five, so the six may be a different scheme. The point that the body holds a whole hidden cosmos is clear.

links.note: Both mock sectarian ranking with the image of one city: 1558's six roads and barking dog, 1568's Nandi laughing at those who name 'this penance, that penance' while all who understand enter the city.
1556 condemns those who stay inside their sect and perish; 1558 says all six sects lead to one city. The road is not the fault; refusing to go beyond it, or attacking the others, is.
Both make worship of the feet the fruit of knowing: the Kural asks what learning has achieved without it, Tirumular says his examining succeeded where the gods' failed because it ended in worship.

1557 says the First Lord moves among the six sects so that they seek his feet (தாளிணை நாட); 2753 counts the hundred and eight sects as means (சாதகமாகும் சமயங்கள்) among the things the Supreme's two feet dance through. Both make the sects instruments the Lord uses, set toward his feet, not rivals to him.

Both liken religious disputants to dogs: in 1558 those who say 'this is good, that is bad' are dogs barking at a hill, in the Thiruppugazh song the disputants who call good words evil and argue against true austerity are like dogs (நாயொப்பவர்). In Tirumular the fault is ranking any of the six roads, in Arunagirinathar it is attacking the true path; the same image serves a plea for tolerance and a plea for protection.

A near-repeat inside the chapter: 1559 opens சைவப் பெருமைத் தனிநாயகன் and calls on all to reach Nandi and be saved (உய்யமினே); 1567 opens சைவ சமயத் தனிநாயகன் நந்தி and says he laid down one guru's path for salvation (உய்ய). 1567 names what 1559 only praises: the Siva path, the sanmarga, set out for those in the world.

Both name the letter ச recited (சகாரத்தை ஓதுமின், ஓதுஞ் சகாரம்) as part of a path: in 731 it joins bindu, ம and nada to make the yogi's path of dharma, in 1564 reciting it with the mind's twoness cast off brings the flame-light on Hara's path. The pair shows the same mantra-letter used in the yoga of the body and in the inner religion.

A near-repeat in the same chapter: both say Hara's path stands beyond what examination (ஆய்ந்துணர், ஆய்ந்தறி) can grasp, and both end with worshipping his red feet with folded hands (சேவடி கைதொழ). 1566 calls the result a bliss for those who plunge in, 1571 says examining that ends in worship saw this life and the next.

2073 sees virgins, the learned, ascetics and contemplatives each in their own enclosure (ஒருசிறை) and says they do not know the Lord's nature; 1568 says Nandi laughs at madmen who give two names, 'this penance' and 'that penance'. Both make the division of religious practice into rival compartments itself the sign of not knowing the Lord.

Both join the downward face (அதோமுகம்) to a garland of heads: 521 speaks of the downward face that bears the cosmos and of him who wears a garland of white skulls (வெண்டலை மாலை); 1569 gives the Lord a downward face beyond his five and a சிரமாலை. 521 supports reading 1569's சிரமாலை as the skull garland rather than a garland on the head.

104 says the First Lord, the jewel-coloured one and the lotus-born are one in continuity, and those who divide them quarrel; 1570 gives the First Lord Vishnu's own deed, measuring the seven worlds (உலகேழும் அளந்தவன்), and names Parasakti as standing undivided (பேதிப்பிலாமை). 1570 applies 104's claim by letting one god's epithet belong to the First Lord.

1540 says people deluded by the deceiver do not know the purpose the body serves (காயம் விளைக்குங் கருத்து); 1572 says the use of the body (உடம்பின் பயன்) cannot be known at all, being set in six unknowable sheaths holding a hidden cosmos. 1572 deepens 1540's charge: the body's purpose escapes not only the deluded but ordinary knowing.

source_issues: 1560: பழிவழி (way of blame) may be a corruption of பழவழி (the old way).
1569: line 4 (நாமே பிரானுக்கு நரரியல் பாமே) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1565: மினற்குறி is read as மின்னல் குறி.
